bio: Associate Professor of Management and Deputy Dean of the College of Business at Al Ain University, UAE. She holds a PhD in Management from the University of Hull, UK. With over a decade of experience in the UAE and Oman, her work focuses on sustainability, leadership, entrepreneurship, and workforce psychology. She contributes to UN-PRME Youth Talks and the PRME Mentorship Program, aligning her teaching with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Gary Smith is a Senior Expert in systems engineering and architecture within the aerospace, defence and security sector, and a Past-President of the International Society for the Systems Sciences. He is also Section Editor for Foundations of Systems Engineering in the Systems Engineering Body of Knowledge (SEBoK). His professional practice spans systems engineering, enterprise and mission architecture, organisational transformation, and integrated business management systems. His interests include systems science, methodological pluralism, organisational cybernetics, system dynamics, Soft Systems Methodology, and the relationship between systems thinking and systems engineering. Gary’s research explores meta-frameworks for organising transversal knowledge about systems, relationships among form, function and fit, and systemic coherence in human-AI collaboration. He is a guest editor for work bringing systems thinking and systems biology into closer dialogue. He contributes regularly to international systems communities, conferences and collaborative research initiatives, seeking to connect foundational systems theory with practical challenges in organisations, engineering, health and society.

Director of the Africa University Research Ethics Committee (AUREC). He has served as a Senior Lecturer and lecturer in the College of Business and Management sciences for 20 years. He is a holder of Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) from the Ruprecht-Karls-University, Heidelberg (Germany).  He is a multi-disciplinary academic who also holds the Masters in Intellectual Property from Africa University; Master’s in Business Intelligence from the Chinhoyi University of Technology, a Master of Business Administration and a Master of Arts in Philosophy from the Azaliah University, Albuquerque, New Mexico (USA) and the University of Zimbabwe respectively. Expertise is in Intellectual Property, Business Intelligence, Management Information Systems, Innovation, Entrepreneurship, International Marketing, Organisational Behaviour, Public Sector Management, Cybernetics, and Dynamic and Integrative Epistemology. Has published over 40 journal articles, 3 book chapters, 3 edited books and 1 monograph. Has supervised to completion 2 doctoral theses and is currently supervising 3 candidates for Africa University, 3 candidates for the University of South Africa (UNISA) and 1 candidate for the management college of South Africa (MANCOSA). He has also supervised over 80 master’s theses and 40 undergraduate dissertations. Has also made presentations at over 70 academic conferences in Africa, Europe and the Americas.

Tadeja Jere Jakulin is Full Professor of Systems Theory in Tourism at the University of Primorska, Faculty of Tourism Studies – Turistica (Portorož, Slovenia), where she serves as Vice Dean for Internationalisation and Quality and heads the Department of Cultural Tourism. She is President of the Slovenian Society for Systems Research and a member of the  AIEST (International Association of Scientific Experts in Tourism). Her research applies general systems theory, systems thinking, cybernetics, and system dynamics to tourism, cultural heritage, and pilgrimage. In her latest research, she began working with the Viable System Model, the Object–Subject–Model epistemological triad, and Peircean semiotics, using the Škofjeloški pasijon -Slovenia's UNESCO-listed passion play -as an empirical case. At Metaphorum 2026, she examines how the VSM illuminates the governance and long-term viability of this living heritage performance. She has published in Kybernetes, PLOS ONE,  Sensors, Brain Sciences and the International Journal of Religious Tourism and Pilgrimage, with chapters for Routledge, Palgrave Macmillan, Springer, and Edward Elgar. She co-edited Law, Humanities, and Tourism (Cambridge Scholars, 2026) and received the 2026 IRTP Lifetime Achievement Award.

Ana Paula Baltazar is an architect, with a Master's from UFMG, a PhD from University College London, and postdoctoral research at UFMG's Faculty of Education. She is an Associate Professor in the Department of Projects, School of Architecture, UFMG, where she coordinates the MOM and Lagear research groups, and led UFMG's Graduate Program in Architecture and Urbanism from 2019 to 2021. A CNPq Research Productivity Fellow since 2014, her current research focuses on the development of interfaces for technical advisory and socio-spatial pedagogy, having human emancipation as its ultimate aim, currently through projects with Yanomami and quilombola communities.

David J. Teece is Professor of the Graduate School at the University of California, Berkeley, Distinguished Scholar of Strategy and Innovation at the University of South Florida’s Muma College of Business, Chairman Emeritus of the Berkeley Research Group, and co-founder and Executive Chairman of Dynamic Experts. He received his PhD in economics from the University of Pennsylvania in 1975, during Stafford Beer’s adjunct professorship at the Wharton School. A scholar-entrepreneur, Professor Teece is best known for originating the Dynamic Capabilities framework, the Dynamic Competition paradigm, and the Profiting from Innovation model, which have shaped research and practice in strategy, innovation, entrepreneurship, and competition policy. His work has been cited more than 269,000 times, making him one of the world's most influential scholars in business and economics. He advises governments and corporations worldwide on strategy, innovation, and technological change. In 2020, Clarivate ranked him the world's most influential scholar in management and named him a Clarivate Laureate in Economics for his contributions to innovation, entrepreneurship, and competition. In 2021, Thinkers50 recognized him as a Distinguished Management Thinker.

PhD Candidate in Systems Engineering at Instituto Politécnico Nacional, Mexico. Her research focuses on Systems Thinking, complex systems, water governance and the dynamics of tourism systems from a transdisciplinary perspective. Her work centres on the study and design of social-ecological systems through the application of methodologies such as the Viable System Model, Soft Systems Methodology and System Dynamics to address challenges related to sustainability and governance. She has published scientific articles in JCR indexed and international journals, as well as book chapters on tourism, sustainability and Systems Thinking. She has presented her research at international conferences, including Metaphorum (Berlin and Manchester) and ISSS (Washington and Birmingham), as well as at several national events, including the International Congress on Applied Tourism Research and the Mexican Academy of Tourism Research. She is a member of Grupo de Investigación en Sistémica y Turismo. Her research integrates Systems Thinking with territorial action to contribute to the design of governance strategies and regenerative solutions for rural communities.

Full Professor at Instituto Politécnico Nacional, Mexico. He founded and teaches on the following postgraduate programmes: the Master's Degree in Tourism Administration and Innovation, the PhD in Systems Engineering, and the PhD in Innovation Management and Policy. He holds a degree in Industrial Engineering, a Master of Science in Systems Engineering, and a PhD in Science specialising in Administrative Sciences. Since 2005, he has been a member of the Sistema Nacional de Investigadores, where he currently holds Level II status. His research focuses on the study and application of the body of knowledge of Systems Science, particularly in the dynamics of complex systems and complexity management. As a result of the consolidation of his research line, he founded the Grupo de Investigación en Sistémica y Turismo in 2012. Through this group, more than 30 basic research projects have been undertaken to address national challenges. He has supervised the graduation of 20 doctoral and 75 master's students. His scholarly output comprises more than 100 research articles published in JCR indexed (Q1, Q2) and Scopus indexed journals, 36 book chapters, one authored book, three edited books, and more than 100 presentations at national and international conferences.

Isaías Badillo-Piña holds a degree in Electrical Engineering and earned both his Master's and PhD degrees in Systems Engineering. He has published more than 30 research articles in JCR indexed (Q1 and Q2) and Scopus indexed journals, as well as more than 15 book chapters with internationally recognised academic publishers. He is a Research Professor in the PhD Programme in Systems Engineering at Instituto Politécnico Nacional, Mexico. His research focuses on Systems Science. He has led more than 5 research projects and has supervised 5 doctoral theses and 4 master's dissertations. He is a member of several prestigious professional and academic associations, including the Asociación Mexicana de Ingenieros Mecánicos y Electricistas, the College of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, the Mexican Institute of Systems and Cybernetics, the Mexican Academy of Systems Science, the Asociación Latinoamericana de Sistemas (Secretary, 2008–2010), the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the ISSS, and the American Production and Inventory Control Society (APICS).

Lien Peeters co-owns (with Benny Corvers) Prepared Mind, a Belgian-Dutch consultancy firm. Both originally trained as linguists and have worked in the field of organisational design and development for the past 15 years. The Viable System Model and Modern Sociotechnical Systems have been at the core of their work ever since they started out. Lien helps turning complex strategic challenges into actionable decisions. She combines a strong structuring ability with a high dose of empathy and pragmatism, making her an ideal sounding board for organizations in transition. She earned her stripes in the world of education, where she held policy and management positions. Prepared Mind’s ambition is to change the world of work by enabling a fundamentally different dialogue within and between organisations, helping clients to design and develop new conditions that will allow their organisations to adjust sustainably. Prepared Mind mainly works with governments and social purpose organisations in youth care, mental health care, education
